summary.text: A neap tide is the point in the lunar cycle when the tide's range, the height gap between high and low water, is at its smallest.
It comes at first and third quarter moon, when the Sun and Moon sit 90° apart as seen from Earth and the Sun's tidal force partly cancels the Moon's.
Neaps bring milder tidal conditions, and they fall about seven days apart from spring tides.

items.prompt: You want to explore a rocky shore on the day the sea rises and falls the least. Which Moon phase should you pick?

options.label: A full moon
A quarter moon
A new moon
Any phase, they are all alike

items.explain: At first and third quarter the tide's range is at its minimum; new and full moon bring the biggest range.

items.prompt: Why is the tide's range weakest around first and third quarter?

options.label: The Moon is at its farthest point from Earth
Earth's spin slows down during those weeks
The Sun's pull, at right angles, partly cancels the Moon's
The Sun's pull switches off for a few days

items.explain: With the Sun and Moon 90° apart as seen from Earth, the solar tidal force partly cancels the lunar one.

items.prompt: Today brings a spring tide. Roughly when will the next neap tide arrive?

options.label: In about a week
Tomorrow
In about a month
In about six months

items.explain: There is about a seven-day interval between springs and neaps.

items.prompt: Compared with a spring-tide day, what does a neap-tide day bring?

options.label: Stronger currents than average
Shorter slack water than average
Only one high water all day
A smaller gap between high and low

items.explain: Neaps have the minimum range and milder conditions; stronger currents and shorter slack water belong to spring tides.

items.prompt: Neap tides are also called quadrature tides. What does that name point to?

options.label: They come four times each month
Each one lasts a quarter of a day
Sun and Moon sit 90° apart from Earth's view
They reach a quarter of normal height

items.explain: Quadrature is the arrangement where the Sun and Moon are separated by 90° as seen from Earth, which is when neaps occur.

items.prompt: A tide chart lists MHWN, short for mean high water neaps. What does it stand for?

options.label: The highest tide that can ever be predicted
The average of high tides on neap-tide days
The average of low tides on neap-tide days
The average sea level over many years

items.explain: MHWN is the average of the two high tides on the days of neap tides.
